name: python-resolve-calls-uses
body:
The Python frontend must resolve references through `ty`'s project semantics against the full project context: a resolved function or method call becomes a Calls edge (Function to Function); a resolved class base becomes a Uses edge to the base class Struct; a resolved class/constructor reference becomes a Uses edge from the calling Function to the class Struct. Declaration hierarchy is emitted as contains edges (module/file to class to method) like every other frontend, and annotations/params are erased the same way (self/cls dropped). Resolution runs against the full `ty` project (the whole scanned tree plus its environment), never a per-file or reduced mode.

Python FQN rendering rule for same-scope duplicate function names (including `@overload` stubs and conditional/redefinition): declarations are still grouped on `(parent, name)` and rendered `parent.name` for a singleton group, `parent.name(T1,T2,...)` for an overloaded group — but because annotations/params are erased, two same-name defs in one scope can erase to identical (or empty) param lists and render the same FQN, which panics in `claim` (src/ingest.rs:88-95). The Python renderer must therefore guarantee uniqueness: when a `(parent, name)` group contains members that erase to the same param list (identical or empty), every member of that colliding subgroup gets the deterministic suffix `#<file-basename>:<start_line>`, i.e. `parent.name(T1,T2,...)#<file-basename>:<start_line>`, mirroring Go's `parent.init#<file-basename>` special case extended with the declaration's 1-based start line (unique within a file). Differently-annotated overloads keep the bare `parent.name(T1,T2,...)` form; a singleton keeps `parent.name`.

AC: a fixture where a.py calls a function defined in b.py yields a Calls edge to b's function; a class subclassing a base in another file yields a Uses edge to the base Struct; a constructor call on a project class yields a Uses edge to that class Struct. Plus a duplicate-name fixture: a `.pyi` with two `@overload` stubs of the same name and identical annotations, and a module with a conditional redefinition of one function name in the same scope — the scan must not panic on an FQN collision, each declaration must appear as a distinct FQN (the colliding subgroup suffixed `#<file-basename>:<start_line>`), and a call to each must resolve to the correct declaration's Function node.
